title: Scroll-driven effects (advanced, support-aware)
learningObjectives: Explain scroll-driven effects (advanced, support-aware) and use visual effects responsibly.

understand.concept: Scroll-driven animations connect animation progress to a scroll timeline or view timeline rather than elapsed time. CSS features include scroll-timeline, view-timeline, and animation-timeline, with browser support that must be checked for the target environment.
understand.whyItMatters: Scroll-driven effects should remain progressive enhancements. Essential content must be visible without the effect, and reduced-motion preferences should be respected. Test performance and browser support before relying on the feature.
understand.analogy: A time-based animation follows a clock; a scroll-driven animation follows how far the reader has moved through content.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; CSS compositing and animation timelines follow browser rendering rules.

explain.narrative: In supporting browsers the bar follows root scroll progress. Without support, the page content remains usable; the progress effect is decorative.

examples.explanation: In supporting browsers the bar follows root scroll progress. Without support, the page content remains usable; the progress effect is decorative.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered example demonstrating the visual effect or animation behaviour.

practise.guidedTask: Experiment with a scroll timeline in a supported browser. Add a static fallback and a reduced-motion rule; document which browsers you tested.
practise.independentTask: Build a visual component using the effect. Include a fallback, check contrast, and test keyboard and reduced-motion behaviour where relevant.
hints: Keep essential content independent of visual effects.
Check browser support and fallback behaviour.

questions.prompt: What controls the progress of a scroll-driven animation?
questions.explanation: Scroll-driven animation progress is linked to a scroll or view timeline.

questions.prompt: What should accompany an advanced visual effect?
options: A readable fallback and accessible content
Essential meaning available only through the effect
An assumption that all browsers support it
questions.answer: A readable fallback and accessible content
questions.explanation: Progressive enhancement keeps the interface usable when effects are unsupported or disabled.
